title: Parameterized Methods for Game Dynamics
summary: We introduce a parameterized computational framework for the evolution of strategic behavior in continuous games. We consider the collective dynamics of players through a time-dependent probability density over the strategy space, representing the likelihood of each strategy being chosen at any given time. Instead of directly solving the high-dimensional Fokker-Planck equation that governs this evolution, we represent the probability density as the pushforward of a reference distribution with parameterized pushforward maps and consider the evolution of the parameterized equations.
